content:
alice_support: FYI — ACME Inc reported an app break after yesterday's DNS migration. Their service `svc.acme.internal` resolves to NXDOMAIN from their VPC and app logs show `dial tcp: lookup svc.acme.internal: no such host`. They can reach public endpoints. @ben_infra can you take a look?

ben_infra: On it. Can you paste the customer VPC id and a simple repro (instance + command)?

eva_csm: VPC is vpc-0a1b2c3d, customer ran `dig svc.acme.internal +short` from an app pod and got nothing. They also tried `curl` and saw TLS cert errors because hostname didn't resolve. Repro steps attached in case notes.

carol_dns: This smells like private hosted zone not associated or a duplicate hosted zone in another account (split-horizon). Ask customer to run: `dig @10.2.1.2 svc.acme.internal +short` (their VPC resolver IP) and `dig @8.8.8.8 svc.acme.internal +short` — compare. Also run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "acme.internal"` in our account and the old account if they migrated.

ben_infra: Got quick dig from customer: `dig @10.2.1.2 svc.acme.internal +short` -> (empty) ; `dig @8.8.8.8 svc.acme.internal +short` -> 34.210.12.45. So public DNS resolves, VPC resolver returns NXDOMAIN. Suggests private zone exists but not associated with this VPC, or there's a resolver rule hijack.

carol_dns: Also check Route53 resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=CreatorRequestId,Values=acme-migration` (or list by name). If there's an outbound/inbound rule pointing to the wrong resolver, that'll shadow.

dan_platform: Another quick check: confirm there isn't a conflicting private hosted zone in a different AWS account with the same name. Private hosted zones are account-scoped; if migration recreated the zone in the wrong account and associated it with 0 VPCs, the VPC will not see it. Run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query "HostedZones[?Name=='acme.internal.']"` in both accounts.

alice_support: I pulled hosted zone list for the migration account and found a private zone `acme.internal` with ID Z-MIGRATE-123 but no VPC associations. Our production account has Z-OLD-789 associated with a different VPC set. Looks like the migration created a new zone and the VPC assoc step failed.

carol_dns: That explains it. If the VPC is not associated with any private hosted zone for that name, the VPC resolver falls back to public (or NXDOMAIN if nothing public), depending on record existence. In this case public resolves to an external IP (the old infra), but internal should point to internal ELB — missing.

ben_infra: Planned remediation: create association between Z-MIGRATE-123 and vpc-0a1b2c3d, then check propagation. Steps: `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z-MIGRATE-123 --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d` (need owner-account permissions). I'll coordinate with ops to run it.

route53-bot: NOTE: Associate-hosted-zone request queued (ticket #INC-4221).

eva_csm: Customer is on standby for a fix, says they can tolerate a brief window. Please advise ETA.

ben_infra: Ops confirmed they can run assoc now, but need a short maintenance window (5-10m) for propagation across resolver caches. Targeting in 20 minutes. I'll post updates.

dan_platform: After assoc, advise customer to flush DNS at app level (restart pods) and confirm with `dig @10.2.1.2 svc.acme.internal +short` and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/*`. Also check client-side caching TTLs.

alice_support: Great. Thanks all — will update ACME support ticket and page them when done.

ben_infra: Done — association completed at 1853456812. Quick verification: `dig @10.2.1.2 svc.acme.internal +short` -> `10.10.5.23` (internal ELB). Customer confirmed app traffic healthy and TLS errors cleared. Marking resolved pending post-mortem.

carol_dns: Post-mortem note: migration runbook must include VPC-hosted-zone-assoc step and validation checks (dig from sample VPC, resolver-rule sanity). I'll draft a runbook item. :white_check_mark:

alice_support: Closing thread after PM drafted. Thanks!
